msg.not_open: The device is not open — press “Open” at the top.
msg.no_layout_hint: There is no layout for this VID:PID: on the “Device” tab you can create one from the HID descriptor.
trig.title: Trigger {nm}
trig.stages_help: Each stage fires when the travel (after the curve) crosses its threshold; the target is a button, key or mouse button (several separated by commas). Together with the “off” mode the trigger becomes purely button-like.
trig.btn_value: {nm} value while a button targeting {nm} is held
prof.prompt_name: Name of the new profile (letters, digits, ._-):
gyro.live_help: Put the gamepad on a table — all three values should be ≈ 0. If not, press “Calibrate zero”. Rotate the gamepad: yaw (left/right) and pitch (up/down) should move the matching bars; if they move the wrong way, use inversion.
dev.mode_switchable: The device is switched by a command from the program; the choice is remembered for this model and the gamepad is reopened.
dev.mode_fixed: This is about the mode of the DEVICE ITSELF (XInput / DInput / DS4). This gamepad cannot be switched from software — only with the buttons/switch on the body or receiver (then press “Refresh” at the top). What games will see — XInput emulation or the native protocol — is chosen in the “Output protocol” card below.
dev.out_help: What games will see: XInput emulation or a virtual device in the gamepad’s “native” protocol.
dev.hs_hidden: original hidden: {n} nodes closed (hidraw/event/js) — SDL and games see only the virtual gamepad
dev.hs_denied: original NOT hidden: the daemon lacks the CAP_FOWNER capability — SDL/games will see both the original and the virtual gamepad
dev.hs_none: no device nodes to hide were found
dev.hide_cb_help: Games will see only the virtual gamepad (no duplicated buttons).
dev.hide_off_warn: ⚠ Hiding is off: every program can see the original. SDL emulators and games (HIDAPI) may hang on a 2.4G receiver in DInput mode or get double input. Enable “Hide the original” and run the daemon with CAP_FOWNER (see below).
dev.win_hide_a: Windows: hiding is done by the HidHide driver — run
dev.hide_linux_help: SDL with HIDAPI (emulators, SDL3 games) reads the original’s hidraw directly: this causes hangs and double input. Automatic setup (udev rules + a systemd service with the CAP_FOWNER capability; it asks for sudo itself). The daemon stays your user and closes the original’s node to other programs itself:
rumble.help: A short test along the same path as in-game rumble. If the motors do not react, the layout has no rumble section.
layout.saved: Saved: {saved}. Layout {id} has been picked up by the daemon.
layout.help: If there is no exact layout, one can be built automatically from the device’s HID descriptor (buttons, sticks, triggers, hat). Linux hidraw only.
btn.help: An empty field means the layout’s default target. Several targets separated by commas (A,RT); NONE disables the button. Keys and mouse: KEY_F, KEY_SPACE, MOUSE_LEFT (other KEY_<key> names work too; access to /dev/uinput is required). The number of simultaneous buttons is not limited.
btn.reset_all_confirm: Reset all buttons to their defaults?
prof.json_help: For advanced users: all profile fields. “Check” compiles it against the device layout and shows warnings without changing anything.
sys.hidden_none: No node is closed right now.
sys.autosetup: Automatic setup (needs sudo, in a terminal):
sys.once_a: One-off start with the hiding capability:
sys.win_note: On Windows hiding is done by HidHide (below).
sys.udev_help: Access to the device without root. Save the output to /etc/udev/rules.d/70-gamepad-remapd.rules and run udevadm control --reload.
sys.hh_help: Commands that hide the original gamepad from games. Run them in an administrator PowerShell (HidHide must be installed).
sys.kb_state: Mode: {mode}; toggle: {toggle}. Enabled by the keyboard section of daemon.json.
sniff.help: Hex inspector: do NOT touch the gamepad for 2.5 s (the idle reference), then press M1–M4/C/Z etc. To teach a button, enter its name and press “Learn”, then hold the button.
stats.note: This is software processing only (parse → map → write). The receiver’s USB polling interval (usually 1–8 ms) is not included.
tp.saved: Saved {saved} (layout {layout}). Auto-detection will open the device by itself.
tp.no_target: no target set in the layout
tp.generated_warn: The layout was built automatically from the HID descriptor: the button names are guesses. Compare them with the labels on the gamepad.
tp.unknown_byte: byte {i}: {from} → {to}  (bits {bits}) — the layout does not know about it
tp.no_reports: no reports yet — press any button (a 2.4 GHz gamepad falls asleep) or try “Find handshake”
tp.idle_hint: Turn the gamepad on and press any button — it will open by itself.
tp.calibrating: calibrating… do not touch the gamepad
tp.title: Gamepad test
tp.hs_hint: For devices that stay silent until they are “woken up”. The program tries the known handshakes from the library (bytes from open-source drivers) one by one and checks whether the report stream comes alive. During the search **press buttons and move the sticks**: a gamepad that is silent at rest will reveal itself this way, and that is how the program knows which handshake woke it. Nothing is saved until you press “Save”.
tp.cal_hint: For gamepads the program does not know (or knows imprecisely). You press the buttons and move the sticks one by one following the prompts, while the program watches which bits and bytes of the report change and builds the layout. If the device is silent, the program tries the known handshakes itself (SDL: Flydigi, 8BitDo, GameSir, Switch). Nothing is saved until you press “Save”.
tp.buttons_hint: Press each button: a tested one turns green. The label is “name in the layout → output target”.
tp.sticks_hint: Rotate each stick in a circle — the sectors you have covered light up.
tp.raw_hint: Changed bytes flash yellow. **Orange** means the byte changed but the layout does not know about it (it may hold a hidden button). Noisy bytes (gyro) can be muted: put the gamepad on a table and press “Calibrate noise”.
